questions.q: What does a RAID log track?
questions.explain: RAID stands for Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies — a running log maintained throughout the project.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a phase gate or milestone review?
options: A formal go/no-go checkpoint between TCM phases
questions.explain: Phase gates give the sponsor and project managers a formal decision point before moving into the next TCM phase, based on entry/exit criteria.

questions.q: Which document states the business case, budget, and the Executive Sponsor's authority for the project?
questions.explain: The Project Charter states the business case, scope, budget, and sponsor authority.

questions.q: Typically, what must happen before a project can move from the Validate phase into Transition?
options: The RAID log must be deleted
User Acceptance Testing must have formally passed
All legacy systems must be decommissioned
questions.explain: Moving from Validate into Transition typically requires UAT to have formally passed as an exit criterion.

questions.q: What did Brightfield Industrial Group's RAID log flag as an early key risk?
options: The CFO was unavailable for the kickoff
The legacy system's export tool had never been tested against the new chart of accounts
Oracle Cloud Success Navigator was unavailable
questions.explain: Brightfield's team logged the untested legacy export tool against the new chart of accounts as a key early risk, revisited throughout data migration.
